newsitem.title: USA: Killer asked to reveal girl's whereabouts.
newsitem.headline: Killer asked to reveal girl's whereabouts.

text.p: Residents of rural upstate New York held a 16-mile walk Tuesday as part of a campaign to convince a killer to disclose where he buried the body of a local 12-year-old girl.
Sentencing for the convicted murderer, Lewis Lent, has been postponed until April 11 in an effort to give him more time to reveal her whereabouts.
Sara Ann Wood disappeared in August 1993 while walking her broken bicycle home from a friend's house. Tuesday would have been her 16th birthday.
"Lewis Lent is the only person who knows where she is, and we want her returned for proper burial," said Frank Williams, who heads a community support group known as Team Sara.
On the walk, Wood's parents and siblings and community members stopped to hold a prayer service at a tree not far from her house in Frankfort, New York, where police found her broken bicycle.
Then they walked through the small towns of Ilion, Mohawk and Herkimer, where Lent is held in the county jail.
They placed 12 red roses -- for the years Sara was alive -- and four white roses -- for the years she has been missing -- at the door of the jail.
Lent once drew a map of the body's whereabouts for state troopers, who spent days digging in frozen ground but never found her.
Supports say they believe Lent knows about their efforts from television and newspaper coverage.
"I am sure he is very aware of what we are doing," Williams said.
